details.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
details.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Paid one-unit rounds; job, input, unit outcomes and lot persist across pauses; resuming pays only the remaining units after revalidation; completion, an unsuitable unit, cancelling and death settle once. No unattended progress.

details.costs: Study: 2 rounds. Prepare: inputStackId is the exact item id of your own edible food stack, quantity the whole units to prepare (at most its whole units); one round and 0.5 energy per unit, so 7 units take 7 rounds and 3.5 energy. Every round is checked before any charge; prepare resumes your paused work (inputStackId and quantity may be omitted). Inspect (inputStackId of your own food) and inspect-progress (your latest preparation): one round, 0.2 energy, no food used. Cancel: one round, no energy. No vessel, water, fuel, tool or ground surface is used or given. Eating and giving use eat and give at their own costs.
details.effects: Each paid round separates one whole unit from the input, checks it by eye and brushes it by hand, held, never set on the ground. A usable unit joins one owned lot of the same food with unchanged quantity, origin, age, decay, nutrition and toxicity, recorded as raw, unheated, dry-brushed, safety unknown. Loose soil on food is not represented, so no debris is measured or removed and no cleanliness is claimed. A spoiled unit is reported unsuitable, stays unprepared and ends the work. Nothing is cooked, peeled, washed, made safe or kept fresher; food keeps ageing, and the planting trial treats prepared units as processed. The lot holds only completed units. Inspections record visible condition, treatment and your own eating record (not a safety test) as an unverified personal record. An unworked round, too little energy, or an input no longer yours with a whole unit pauses without charge. Cancel or death ends the work; completed units stay. No refund or reward; nobody is fed.

execution.progress: trial pays the setup in its first round and the working round in the next round of the same action; resume does a paused working round.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds, 0.2 energy each. inspect: inputStackId (your own item), optional operation, quantity, implementId, supportId; 1 round, 0.2 energy, no food used; reports condition, structure, means, limits and unmet needs. trial: the same fields; round 1 is the setup (0.2) and reserves the portion, round 2 of the same action the working round (0.5): 0.7 energy a bout. open: quantity 0.1-1 in tenths (default the item, up to 1); cut: quantity 1. inspect-progress: 1 round, 0.2. resume does the unpaid working round after fresh checks; cancel: 1 round, no energy. Refusals cost nothing; getting a stone and travel are separate actions.
details.effects: open needs a represented shell (here hazelnut); each 0.1 block gets one squeeze or impact. Bare hands press with the bounded hand force of hand-break-food@1 over one unit; an implement (own whole rigid inedible piece) struck on a support (solid inedible object in reach, not a plant or animal, or another own piece on firm ground) passes the lower of their strengths (hardness / 10) x (1 - flexibility). At or below the shell strength nothing changes; above it damage (load - strength) / strength stays on the item: below 1 cracked and closed, at 1 open, then picked apart by hand into 0.1 kernel and 0.1 shell per block with the source origin, age and decay; the kernel keeps all food value; shell is not food. cut: a whole unit without a shell, an own stone or flint edge passing the world contact model (index 8+ and at least the food, radius 0.0002 or less, sound) and a support; one stroke parts it once more (up to 10 portions), still one unit with mass, food value and age unchanged, eaten whole; no offcut. peel is refused: no separable layer is represented. Wear: an implement no harder than what it meets, or a support softer by 0.5, loses 0.0001 kg per contact (2 at most per block or stroke); nothing breaks. Another action, lost reach or means or low energy pause before the working round; a changed portion ends the work; cancel or death releases it once. Safety, toxins and nutrition stay unknown; no refund or reward.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
